To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Denmark has reduced its carbon dioxide emissions per capita by about 30% from 1990 to 2008.

(1) Denmark's efforts to curb its carbon emissions have been successful, but the results of this effort have been influenced by changes in Denmark's trade with other countries; (2) the consumption emissions of Denmark's trade have increased substantially, largely due to the growth of Denmark's trade with China; and (3), measures of consumption emissions that are robust to changes in the availability of information about trade are important for evaluating the success of environmental policies.
the carbon emissions of Denmark have been reduced since 1990.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects that international trade has on the consumption emissions of small, open economies.
the effects of international trade on carbon emissions in Denmark and other small, open economies that have implemented environmental policies.
the effects of international trade on the environment and the effects that environmental policy can have on international trade.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, although Denmark has been very successful in reducing its carbon emissions, its efforts are not sufficient to achieve its goal of a 20% reduction in carbon emissions by 2020.
Denmark has been able to reduce its carbon dioxide emissions by 20% since 1990 while experiencing a 50% increase in real GDP.
the Danish experience indicates that the effects of international trade on the environment should not be ignored.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
international trade has a significant influence on the outcome of Denmark efforts to reduce its consumption emissions.
Denmark's efforts to curb carbon emissions have had mixed results.
, in the context of Denmark, the consumption-based approach to carbon emissions is more informative than the production-based approach.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of trade on consumption emissions should be considered when evaluating the outcomes of environmental policies.
small, open economies should consider both consumption and production emissions when evaluating the outcome of their efforts to reduce carbon dioxide.
the effects of international trade on carbon emissions should not be ignored in the development and evaluation of environmental policy.
